title: Playbook
description: A named binding of a strategy to concrete participants, plus the deployment-specific bits (check target, budgets). Resolved and snapshotted at run start so editing this file cannot alter an in-flight run.

strategyVersion.description: Pin. A run refuses to start if the on-disk strategy has a different version.

participants.description: Keys must exactly match the strategy's roles — every role bound, no extras.

effort.description: Validated against that model's efforts AND the harness's effort capability. An unsupported combination is a load-time error, not a runtime surprise.

instructions.description: Optional role instructions file, relative to the playbook.

fallbackModels.description: Optional roster allowlist for automatic quota substitutions. Omitted preserves default selection; an empty list disables substitution. Does not change the initially assigned seats.

checks.description: A playbook may STRENGTHEN the strategy's requirement (none -> optional -> required), never weaken it. A project that cannot be verified is not a reason to weaken a strategy that depends on verification — pick a different strategy.

concurrent.description: Run the revision's checks while its reviewers review (default true). A failed check still sends the candidate back for another round; false runs checks before the reviews start.

budgets.description: May only tighten the strategy's budgets.

maxCostUsd.description: Ceiling on KNOWN cost in USD. Steps whose provider reports no price are counted separately and cannot be capped.

overrides.description: Narrow, explicit strategy overrides — loop round counts and the like. Dotted paths; the loader rejects any path outside an allow-list.

autoClose.description: Opting in to closing on review alone. Absent means the strategy's default applies, which is 'verified'.

justification.description: Required when lowering to review-only, so the choice is recorded rather than inherited silently.

intent.description: Default intent for runs of this playbook: an overlay defined by the strategy under intents/. A run may choose another through runOptions.intent.

workspace.description: Per-playbook workspace choices. The base, symlink policy and isolation may be chosen here; clean-base rules are the strategy's.

excludes.description: Paths left out of the base snapshot (git pathspec globs relative to the checkout, e.g. runtime, config, **/node_modules): runtime state, secrets and dependency trees that are not source and would otherwise be committed into the base. Absent from the worktree entirely. Before snapshot selection v1 only working-tree bases applied them; under v1 (fence.selection: 1) they hold for every base policy and inside materialized links.

isolation.description: 'in-place' works directly in the project checkout: no worktree, no patch, edits land live. Normally chosen per run (runOptions.isolation).

materializeGrants.description: Snapshot selection v1: materialization targets allowed although they are not owned by a project this panel resolves. Each grant names a directory (absolute); a target inside it is copied under the owner's selection when it has a Git owner, whole otherwise. Anything else outside a known project is refused before copying.

reconcile.description: Project setting only (projects/<id>.yaml; refused in a playbook). Per-path policy for `reconcile-delivery`, which merges an approved patch three-way onto source that drifted on the patch's own paths (docs/execution-contract.md "Reconciling a delivery with drifted source"). Keys are worktree-relative paths or globs; `append` resolves a merge conflict on such a path by keeping the source's content and appending the lines the candidate added there (only when the candidate's change to it is pure addition), `prepend` the same before it. Every other conflict, and any change to the reviewed delta outside these paths, refuses the reconciliation. The object form `{ rule, inert: true }` also declares the path inert: when all the drift is on inert paths and every other path is byte-identical to the approved revision, the approved revision's check result carries and no check runs. The first entry naming a path decides both. Declaring a path inert makes it the project's responsibility that no check depends on that file (docs/project-infrastructure.md "Reconcile policy: inert paths").

related.description: Phase 2 of the seat-access fence: other projects a run's seats may read. Each is exported at run start as a read-only snapshot of what its repository carries (no history, no ignored files) and mounted read-only in the seat fence; it is never part of the candidate and is removed when the workspace is released.

delivery.description: Delivery may save a patch, commit a candidate, or apply approved changes to source. Implementation playbooks allow an explicit patch-only choice.

hostRef.description: Reference only — never an inline host/credential. ssh-config:<name> defers entirely to the user's ~/.ssh/config.

identityRef.description: agent: uses the running ssh-agent; no key material is read or stored.

materialize.description: How the candidate content reaches the target. Whatever is sent must reproduce the exact revision fingerprint on arrival, or the check result is rejected as not bound to the revision.

required.description: A failing non-required command is recorded but does not fail the check set.

timeoutSecondsPerFilter.description: Only on a modules tier test or browser template holding `{{filters}}`: seconds added to `timeoutSeconds` for each filter the one command receives, so its bound grows with the number of affected modules.

kind.description: SSH targets only (0e). candidate: the whole run text executes as the target's unit user inside a bubblewrap allow-list (read-only /usr, /etc and /sys, private /tmp, an empty home with only confinement.readOnly/writable, the candidate directory), in a transient unit; privileged: runs as the SSH account with the candidate and control directories masked, so it can manage units and read host logs but cannot read or execute candidate files. Absent: unconfined, labelled remote-unconfined.

network.description: candidate only: keep the host network (dependency installation). Otherwise the unit has a private network namespace.

service.description: candidate only: start the unit and return; the engine stops it after the finalizers. Its unit name is exported to every command as DEVPANEL_UNIT_<ID>.

join.description: candidate only: the id of an earlier candidate service without network. The command enters that running service's own user and mount namespaces (its exact fenced view, found by the engine through systemd, never through a file the candidate wrote) and its private network: readiness probes and CLI selftests that inspect the application's processes and sockets.

unprivilegedPorts.description: candidate only, private network: allow binding ports below 1024 inside the unit's own namespace (a fixed engine command).

startedMarker.description: service only: a file, relative to the candidate directory, that the service writes when it has started. The start command then passes only when the unit is active and this file exists, and fails naming the marker and the bound otherwise, so a command after it never races the service's own first writes. Absent: the service counts as started once its unit is up. See docs/project-infrastructure.md "When a service counts as started".

startedTimeoutSeconds.description: startedMarker only: how long the start command waits for the marker, from when the unit is up. It comes on top of timeoutSeconds, which covers the launch.

needs.description: Earlier commands this one depends on (a join implies its service). After a required command fails, a command runs only if it declares needs (an empty list: independent) and every need passed; without needs it is skipped, and a skipped required command leaves the run's outcome unknown. Not allowed on finallyCommands, which always run.

reportsUnavailable.description: Required commands only: this command may say the drive cannot be made (a pinned snapshot it cannot obtain) by exiting non-zero with a line `devpanel-unavailable: <reason>`. The check result is then unavailable, not failed, with the reason in its error, unless another required command failed. Without the line a non-zero exit is an ordinary failure. Declare it only on a command that runs no candidate code: candidate code could otherwise block the check instead of failing it. See docs/project-infrastructure.md "One application snapshot per run".

report.description: Declares what the command's stdout carries; changes nothing about how it runs. selftest: one `== <path>/selftest.report` line followed by that file's JSON (an older spelling with a site prefix, `<site>-selftest`, is read the same). When the command passed, the engine reads the failed tests from it and compares them with the base by test name: a failure the base does not have fails the check (gatingResult), an unreadable report while failures are listed fails it too, inherited failures do not.

kind.description: How checks are executed. An absent target means there is no mechanism at all, which yields an 'unavailable' RESULT — it never rewrites the requirement.

finallyCommands.description: Cleanup and log collection, attempted even after command failure or cancellation; each retains its own timeout.

confinement.description: SSH targets: how kind: candidate commands are confined.

user.description: The unit user; when the SSH account is root the candidate directory is handed to it after arrival is verified. Without it, the host settings' testDrive.confinement.user; with neither, a kind: candidate command is refused.

home.description: The unit user's home, an empty tmpfs inside the fence. Without it, the host settings' testDrive.confinement.home.

readOnly.description: Toolchain paths bound read-only (e.g. the unit user's ~/.nvm).

writable.description: Paths bound writable (e.g. a package cache). Never secrets.

projectRoot.description: SSH targets: the environment's own project root, which the confinement probe must prove invisible to candidate commands.

compareBaseline.description: Run the same commands on the run's base commit eagerly, once per run, concurrently with the first candidate check, and give reviewers a per-command line diff of stdout (base vs candidate). Without it the base is still captured, after the first failed candidate check, to tell inherited (baseline-known) failures from new ones. Doubles the first check's load on the target; off by default.

timing.description: When the target runs. every-revision (default for a playbook target): each new revision, beside its reviews. approved: only a revision every reviewer approved; a failure sends the author another round. For an expensive target (a staging test drive) approved skips the checks of revisions the reviewers send back anyway.

retryFailed.description: How many times a failed check runs again on the same revision before the failure counts. Every attempt is recorded; a pass after a failure is marked flaky.

classifyUnstable.description: Whether a selftest that recorded drives classify as unstable stops gating (execution-contract.md "Unstable selftests"). false: its new failure gates like any other. Drives are recorded either way.

smoke.description: Ids of commands and finallyCommands that make the smoke tier. It runs on every recorded revision beside the reviews, and a failure sends the author another round. The full tier is the whole target, run once on the approved revision; only it counts for closure. Implies timing: approved.

continueSmoke.description: Whether the full drive continues the smoke's running instance when it can be proved unchanged: it executes only the commands the smoke did not run, in declared order, then every finalizer. Set false when a command declared before a smoke service is one the service depends on at boot or needs it down, or when a smoke finalizer changes application data.

keepSeconds.description: How long a passing smoke's instance waits for the full drive before a timer on the target removes it. Past it the full drive runs from scratch.

targeted.description: Named selftests on a repair revision, in place of its smoke, when the previous revision's failed drive or the open findings name failing tests. The result gates the round as a smoke does and never counts for closure: only the full drive does.

command.description: Id of the required, non-service command of the target whose `run` the template replaces; it keeps its kind, needs, position and timeout.

run.description: The command template: `command word... {{tests}} word...`: single spaces between plain words, a literally named program that is no shell builtin and does not exist to run its arguments, and `{{tests}}` once as a word of its own, replaced by the test names, each shell-quoted. Validation refuses anything else, which belongs in a script the template calls. A called program that parses its arguments again defeats that quoting.

always.description: Ids of the commands and finallyCommands that always run with it, in declared order. Everything the tier's commands need or join, and a `report: selftest` command, must be among them or be the template's own command.

maxTests.description: More names than this: the revision runs its smoke.

modules.description: The modules tier (docs/project-infrastructure.md "The modules tier"): the per-revision check of coding playbooks on a Boilerplate project. Each drive runs, in this order: lint of the revision's changed .mjs/.vue files, load of the candidate into the stage instance, restart, readiness, one `test` command per affected module and per core directory (and one `browser` command per affected module when declared), then finallyCommands. No base drive and no baseline comparison: a failing affected-module test blocks the revision. In base-instance mode (no `instance`) a drive holds every drive slot of its stage host; with `instance` the tier runs on an instance of the run's own. The test slot or a finalizer must declare `report: selftest`; a passing drive whose report names a failed test, or shows none, gates failed. No declared id may be a generated `<test.id>-<n>` or `<browser.id>-<n>`.

collections.description: Top-level directory names that are collections (`*` matches any run of characters, e.g. `@*`, `*-modules`). A module is `<collection>/<module>/`; every other path is core.

rootFilter.description: The selftest filter a change at the repository root gets (the root's own core selftests). Default `.`.

lint.description: The project's lint command over the revision's changed .mjs/.vue files: `command word... {{files}} word...` (the targeted template's rules), each file shell-quoted. Left out of a drive with no such files.

load.description: Loads the candidate (the drive's archived directory, the command's working directory) into the project's stage instance, which keeps running it.

restart.description: Restarts the stage instance on the loaded candidate.

ready.description: Waits, bounded, until the restarted instance is ready.

test.description: The framework's selftest CLI for one filter: `command word... {{filter}} word...`; run once per affected module (filter `<collection>/<module>`) and per core directory, the filter shell-quoted as one argument. Ids are `<id>-<n>`. With `{{filters}}` in place of `{{filter}}` it runs ONCE (`<id>-1`) and receives every filter, each shell-quoted as an argument of its own, modules first (those that failed in the run's previous drive leading), then core directories.

browser.description: Optional: the browser scenarios of one module, `{{filter}}` as for test; run once per affected module. `{{filters}}` runs it once with every affected module.

finallyCommands.description: Log and report collection, attempted after every drive.

instance.description: A stage instance per run (docs/project-infrastructure.md "A stage instance per run"). With it the tier runs on an instance of the run's own instead of the one fixed instance: the first drive creates it from the candidate and starts it in place of load and restart, later drives of the run load into it, and the engine destroys it when the run ends or pauses. Every command of the tier names it with `{{instance}}` (its root, `<root>/<name>`) or `{{instanceName}}`; the name is derived from the run id. A drive then takes no drive slot: the host is bounded by the host settings' testDrive.maxInstances. Without `instance` the tier is the base-instance mode: one fixed instance, and a drive holds the staging host whole.

root.description: The directory on the staging host that holds the instances; `{{instance}}` is `<root>/<name>`.

max.description: The stage's own cap of instances, when it is below the host settings' testDrive.maxInstances: the lower of the two applies.

create.description: Creates the instance from the candidate (the drive's archived directory, the command's working directory). Starts nothing.

unavailableExitCodes.description: Exit statuses that mean the instance cannot be created from this candidate (a dependency change that needs an install): the check is `unavailable` with the reason, not failed, and nothing is tested elsewhere.

unavailableReason.description: What such an exit means, said on the check result.

start.description: Starts the created instance; the tier's `ready` then waits for it.

busyExitCodes.description: Exit statuses that mean the stage runs its cap of instances: the command is asked again until it answers otherwise, a wait that is not charged to the wall clock, never a failure.

busyRetrySeconds.description: How long between two such attempts. Default 20.

destroy.description: Stops and removes the instance. Run by the engine, outside any drive, only while the instance's root exists: at the run's end or pause, after a drive that left the instance in doubt, and for an instance whose owner is gone. Default bound 300 s.

gc.description: Optional: removes what no run holds on the stage host. Run once when the panel starts, after the instances of dead owners were destroyed. It names no instance.

tier.description: Set by the engine on the target of one tier's drive; never configured.

files.description: Files on the target whose content hashes are part of the key (the application snapshot identity), read over SSH for an ssh target. A project's testDrive names them through stagingFiles instead.

environment.description: A read-only command run on the target as the SSH account (locally for a local target), never inside a candidate; the sha256 of its stdout is the environment identity (host, installed runtimes, anything else the drive depends on).

maxEntries.description: Entries kept per project; the oldest beyond it are pruned.

maxAgeDays.description: Entries older than this are pruned.

baselineCache.description: Reuse the base drive across runs (issues/<project>/.baselines/). The key is exact: base commit, the tier target's definition hash, these files' content hashes and the environment command's output hash. A component that cannot be computed means no lookup and no store.
